items.title: Three teenagers injured after flag hits high-voltage power line during Kedah procession
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: Three teenagers were injured after a flag carried during the Tokong Sayur procession allegedly came into contact with a high-voltage power line in Mergong here tonight. The flag, reportedly held by one of the teenagers, was blown by strong winds during light rain before coming into contact with the power line, causing all three teenagers to fall. Mergong Tokong Sayur Association secretary Chah Boon Chuan said the annual procession was being held today, with tonight marking its fourth day.

items.title: France accuses Musk of 'online harassment' of Europe leaders
items.summary: PARIS: France's foreign minister on Tuesday accused the billionaire tycoon and owner of the X social media platform Elon Musk of "online harassment" of European leaders, as he sounded the alarm over the risks of interference in the French 2027 presidential election. But Barrot also took aim at the "massive online harassment campaigns by Elon Musk against European leaders, aimed at influencing national debates by exploiting the viral nature of his social network." Barrot vowed that France would hit back.

items.title: Communications Ministry, Global Sumud Movement to produce 'Sumud Protocol' mini-series
items.summary: BANGI: The Communications Ministry will collaborate with the Global Sumud Movement to produce a television mini-series on the "Sumud Protocol" to raise public awareness, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the production was among several initiatives through which the government would support the efforts of Sumud Nusantara and the Global Sumud Flotilla (GSF). Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's presence at the Sumud Nusantara Dinner tonight sent a clear signal that Malaysia's support for Palestinian liberation went beyond political rhetoric and diplomatic discussions.

items.title: Youths aged 30 and below rack up RM5.4bil in BNPL transactions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Young people aged 30 and below recorded 65.9 million buy now, pay later (BNPL) transactions worth RM5.4 billion in the first half of 2026, accounting for 37.9 per cent of total transactions nationwide. In a written reply published on Parliament's website today, the Finance Ministry said Malaysia recorded 173.9 million BNPL transactions worth RM14.7 billion during the period. As at June 30, their outstanding BNPL financing stood at RM2.4 billion, while non-performing financing amounted to RM96.8 million, or four per cent of the outstanding balance.

items.title: Asian refiners set to make hay as Mideast exports pick up
items.summary: Asian refiners look set to be among the biggest beneficiaries of a sustained recovery in Middle Eastern crude oil exports. However, Middle Eastern fuel exports remain at less than half of pre-war levels due to damage to regional refineries. Asia holds around 37 per cent of global refining capacity, according to the Energy Institute, and refiners in India, China, South Korea and Singapore are well placed to capture the value attached to turning crude into petrol, diesel and jet fuel.

items.title: Marriage to Malay does not change foreign spouse's ethnicity, says Saifuddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Marriage between a Muslim foreign national and a Malaysian of Malay descent does not change the foreign spouse's ethnicity to Malay, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the National Registration Department (NRD) would not change the foreign national's ethnicity based on the marriage, which does not alter the individual's original ethnic background. Saifuddin stated in a written reply in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday that the marriage of a Muslim foreign national to a Muslim Malay in the country will not change their original ethnic status.

items.title: NZ First's culture war push hits wall
items.summary: Winston Peters, the veteran leader of New Zealand First, has borrowed heavily from the culture-war playbook that has energised populist parties across the English-speaking world, railing against "woke" politics, gender policy and high immigration ahead of next month's general election. Given current tight polling and New Zealand's proportional representation voting system, Luxon's National Party will need the seats of New Zealand First and the right-wing ACT party for a chance to form the government again and keep the country on its conservative track. "This time it's almost now or never in terms of getting far greater power to implement our alternative to how to run an economy," said Peters, 81, arguing voters had previously given New Zealand First only limited power.

items.title: NST Leader: Cable thefts pose a grave national threat
items.summary: MALAYSIAN public spaces and homes are so laden with prized assets and objects that they constantly attract thieves who steal and fence valuables with ease. Years ago, thieves favoured steel manhole covers and brass water meters from residential homes. Now, thieves target public utility and industrial cables, made valuable by surging copper and metal prices.

items.title: Government settles RM17.15bil in excess tax refunds as at Sept 30
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has settled RM17.15 billion in excess tax refunds involving 3.23 million taxpayer cases as at Sept 30, 2026. In a written reply published on Parliament's website today, the Finance Ministry said RM6.38 billion had been refunded to 3.1 million individual taxpayers, while RM8.95 billion went to more than 130,000 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The ministry said the Inland Revenue Board had implemented measures to improve tax refund processing, including allocating refunds based on the age of outstanding cases and prioritising MSMEs and companies facing cash flow difficulties.

items.title: Salam submarine cable project to begin in 2027
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had issued an invitation for the project and was evaluating it. The project aims to strengthen communications connectivity between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak. Meanwhile, Phase Two of the Jendela (National Digital Network) project is expected to begin in November, covering 1,000 sites nationwide, including 352 in Sabah.

items.title: Whirlwind videos showing cars lifted into air go viral
items.summary: The video, posted on Threads by user @zhaeim, showed a blue Perodua Alza briefly lifted into the air before crashing into a white Perodua Ativa in the adjacent lane. Another car farther ahead appeared to hover briefly as the whirlwind moved back and forth before dissipating during the thunderstorm. "Thunderstorm in the Kota Damansara area, oh God, the whirlwind is scary.

items.title: Squishy toy raid: Over 2,300 uncertified toys seized without MC mark
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: The Terengganu Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has seized 2,380 squishy toys worth RM30,391 over suspected non-compliance with safety standards since Oct 3. Its director, Mohd Mufsi Lat, said the soft, sponge-like toys, which came in various shapes and designs, were seized following 101 inspections across the state. "Action was taken against six premises in Kuala Terengganu, with investigations opened under the Consumer Protection Act 1999 and regulations governing toy safety standards.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1554759]] [[nid:1554758]] [[nid:1554757]] [[nid:1554756]] [[nid:1554755]] [[nid:1554754]] [[nid:1554753]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Sabah schools to close if API exceeds 150 for three consecutive days
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Schools in Sabah will be temporarily closed if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 150 for three consecutive days, the state government has announced. State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, who is also State Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the measure was taken to protect pupils and teachers from the adverse health effects of haze. All schools in Tawau have been ordered to close from tomorrow amid worsening haze conditions.

items.title: Anwar expresses 'utter disgust' over international community's failure on Palestine
items.summary: BANGI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed deep disappointment over the international order's failure to address the Palestinian cause, describing it as a failure to uphold democracy and human rights. Anwar questioned the consistency of the international community in upholding these principles, saying Palestinians should not be subjected to different standards of treatment. Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Sumud Nusantara Command Centre director-general Datuk Dr Ahmad Sani Araby.

items.title: Trailer driver killed in Batu Pahat crash
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A trailer driver was killed after his vehicle rear-ended a lorry on the North-South Expressway near Ayer Hitam. The trailer was carrying wooden pallets, while the lorry was transporting a skylift. Abd Rahim said the trailer hit the rear of the lorry, causing the wooden pallets to crush the trailer's cab and trapping the driver.

items.title: MRR2 flyover accident: Soldier dies after falling onto motorcyclist near TBS
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief assistant commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the incident occurred at 8.04am as the 24-year-old soldier was travelling from his home in Bukit Jalil to his workplace at Sungai Besi Camp. The soldier was thrown onto the road below, while his motorcycle remained on the flyover. "The victim landed on a 46-year-old man riding a Honda Vario motorcycle from Cheras towards Sungai Besi, causing both to fall onto the road.

items.title: Govt urged to clarify police body camera rollout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has been urged to explain the status of the nationwide rollout of police body cameras. Kepong member of parliament Lim Lip Eng said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had informed him in a parliamentary reply in October 2023 that the cameras were expected to be fully deployed by the first quarter of 2025. Lim also urged police to ensure that all searches had a clear legal basis.

items.title: Lorry driver in 12-vehicle crash released on bail
items.summary: His lawyer, Rohan Singh, said the bail was settled through two sureties after proceedings in two separate courts concluded this afternoon. The courts set bail at RM9,000 with one surety for the charge of driving under the influence of drugs and RM3,900 with one surety for the drug consumption charge. Deputy public prosecutor Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan sought bail of RM15,000 and requested that Agilan's driving licence be suspended.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 13, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: MyEG revenue probe Police are investigating the failure to transfer more than RM230.9 million in government revenue involving two MyEG Group companies. Umno denies involvement Umno denies involvement in Negri Sembilan's adat and royal dispute, saying politicians should not interfere. Royal family sues banks A Terengganu royal family member is suing two banks to recover RM1.985 million allegedly lost through unauthorised transactions.

items.title: Pantech Global unit to dispose of freehold land for RM31.73mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pantech Global Bhd's wholly-owned subsidiary, Pantech Steel Industries Sdn Bhd, has entered into a sale and purchase agreement with Veltrix Land Sdn Bhd for the sale of a parcel of freehold land at a total consideration of RM31.73 million. "The proposed disposal is undertaken pursuant to the group's revised development plans for its Klang operations. Pantech Global added that the proposed disposal will enable the group to recover the capital outlay deployed for the property and redeploy the relevant funds towards the group's ongoing development and operational requirements.

items.title: Anwar calls for stronger federal-state ties under National Covenant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The federal and state governments must strengthen cooperation under the proposed National Covenant framework to ensure more sustainable, equitable and balanced development, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. The proposed covenant aims to strengthen federal-state cooperation and promote more inclusive development and public well-being. "Amid global economic uncertainties, national growth projections and fluctuations in global oil prices, the budget must continue to protect the people, address the rising cost of living and take into account each state's priorities, including border security, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak," he said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: Binasat proposes private placement of up to 60.43mil shares
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Telecommunications engineering solutions provider Binasat Communications Bhd has proposed a private placement of up to 60.43 million new shares, representing up to 10 per cent of its total issued shares, to third-party investors to raise funds. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the gross proceeds from the proposed private placement are estimated at RM4.23 million, while RM21.83 million from the equity-funded portion of its previous placement and share issuance would be reallocated under a proposed variation in the utilisation of proceeds. This would bring the total funds involved to RM26.06 million, of which RM25.75 million is earmarked for the proposed utilisation of proceeds.

items.title: Convicted Myanmar citizens must serve sentences before repatriation
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: Myanmar citizens convicted of criminal offences must complete their sentences in Malaysia before being repatriated, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said although the Myanmar government was prepared to accept its citizens currently held at Immigration detention depots in Malaysia, they would first undergo screening. The remaining 3,600 Myanmar citizens are expected to be repatriated in stages," he said.

items.title: Fitch: Malaysia's 2027 Budget deficit target hinges on revenue, subsidies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's plan to narrow its fiscal deficit to 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2027 faces pressure from elevated subsidy costs and social spending, Fitch Ratings said. The 2026 deficit target was initially set at 3.5 per cent of GDP, but higher subsidy costs pushed revised expenditure nearly six per cent above the original budget. Under the 2027-2029 Medium-Term Fiscal Framework (MTFF), the government targets an average fiscal deficit of 3.1 per cent of GDP, compared with 3.2 per cent under the previous 2026-2028 framework.

items.title: Police: Two investigation papers opened over RM350,000 bribery claim against senior MACC officer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Two separate investigation papers have been opened into allegations that a senior Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer received a bribe of RM350,000 from an individual in 2017. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the investigations were initiated following a police report lodged over the matter, which had gone viral on several social media platforms. Kumar said the investigation is being conducted under Section 500 of the Penal Code for defamation, which carries a maximum penalty of two years’ jail, a fine, or both upon conviction.

items.title: Former Perak Immigration prosecution chief to begin three-year jail term for corruption
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A former Perak Immigration Department Prosecution Unit chief began serving a three-year prison sentence today after the Court of Appeal reinstated his conviction for soliciting and accepting bribes 11 years ago. A three-member panel led by Judge Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, in an unanimous decision, allowed the prosecution's final appeal to set aside the Ipoh High Court's decision that had acquitted Zaidi Dali, 58. "The conviction recorded by the Sessions Court judge is reinstated.

items.title: Haze expected to ease over next two weeks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The transboundary haze that has affected Malaysia's air quality since Aug 8 is expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks as wind patterns change, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said. He said Malaysia entered the monsoon transition phase on Oct 9, with the northeast monsoon expected to begin towards the end of this month. Syed Ibrahim was responding to concerns raised by Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who described the haze as a national crisis affecting public health, safety, the economy and public well-being.

items.title: Myanmar refugees convicted of offences must serve sentence in Malaysia before repatriation, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 13 — Myanmar refugees convicted of criminal offences must complete their sentences in this country before being repatriated to their home country. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said although the Myanmar government is prepared to accept back its citizens currently held in Immigration detention depots here, screening will be conducted first before such action is taken. “The Myanmar government has agreed to accept back its citizens who are here following our screening process, if our records show they were involved in legal violations, we will handle the legal proceedings first,” he said.

items.title: Anwar calls for stronger federal-state cooperation under National Covenant framework
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The federal and state governments must strengthen cooperation under the proposed National Covenant framework to ensure more sustainable, equitable and balanced development, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. The proposed covenant aims to strengthen federal-state cooperation and promote more inclusive development and public well-being. “Amid global economic uncertainties, national growth projections and fluctuations in global oil prices, the budget must continue to protect the people, address the rising cost of living and take into account each state’s priorities, including border security, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak,” he said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: [UPDATED] Man arrested in Indonesia with 4kg syabu is not Malaysian student
items.summary: Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations confirmed that the suspect arrested by Indonesian authorities was Indonesian, not Malaysian as claimed in circulating reports. He said the man was detained by Tanjung Balai police in North Sumatra on Oct 10 after arriving at Teluk Nibung Ferry Terminal from Port Dickson, Negri Sembilan. "Preliminary investigations found that Indonesian authorities detained an Indonesian man who had arrived at the Teluk Nibung Ferry Terminal from Port Dickson.

items.title: Sime Darby to appeal RM150.18mil tax assessments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sime Darby Bhd said its wholly owned subsidiary, Sime Darby Holdings Bhd (SDHB), will appeal against tax assessments totalling RM150.18 million, including penalties, issued by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) for the years of assessment 2017 to 2023. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Sime Darby said SDHB received the notices of assessment on Sept 30, 2026, after the IRB determined that interest income from SDHB's treasury activities was taxable under Section 4(c) of the Income Tax Act 1967. "It intends to appeal and initiate legal proceedings to challenge the basis and validity of the notices issued by the IRB," Sime Darby said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Ex-pilot with drug record, foreign woman identified in Laos private jet drug probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police have identified two Filipinos, including a former pilot, believed to be linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate behind the seizure of 521kg of methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos. Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the former pilot had chartered the aircraft through a Malaysian broker, while the woman was believed to have acted as the syndicate's coordinator. Hussein said the latest findings followed investigations into the seizure at Luang Prabang International Airport on Oct 1, which also led to the detention of a Malaysian second officer.

items.title: Cross-border haze to ease in two weeks as monsoon transition begins, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The cross-border haze that has affected Malaysia’s air quality since August 8 is expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks as wind patterns change, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said. He said Malaysia had entered the monsoon transition phase on October 9, with the northeast monsoon expected to begin towards the end of this month. Syed Ibrahim was responding to concerns raised by Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who described the haze as a national crisis affecting public health, safety, the economy and public well-being.

items.title: Haze: Kedah schools to operate as usual tomorrow as API readings remain moderate
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 13 — All schools in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings across the state remaining below 100 as of 2pm today. In a statement, the Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said any decisions on school closures or reopening due to the haze would be subject to the Education Ministry’s directives, based on JPN’s monitoring of daily API readings and local developments. “Kedah JPN will continue to monitor the situation and coordinate with the District Education Offices and schools to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel,” it added.

items.title: Home Ministry to seek details on five Malaysians held in Japan drug bust, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 13 — The Home Ministry will contact Japanese authorities to obtain accurate information on the arrest of Malaysians suspected of involvement in a drug case in Japan. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he had instructed Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan to act immediately to establish the facts. However, he said destinations in Japan, including Tokyo, were not included in the original list of hotspots.

items.title: Businessman sentenced to six months’ jail, ordered to pay RM5,000 for assaulting ex-girlfriend
items.summary: Magistrate Amira Sariaty Zainal imposed the sentence on Hoh Peng Onn, 47, after the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt at the end of the defence case. The accused must also pay RM5,000 in compensation to the victim, taking into account the trauma, injuries and emotional distress she suffered,” Amira Sariaty said. The court also ordered that Hoh serve an additional two months in jail if he failed to pay the compensation today.

items.title: Budget 2027: Malaysia’s 3.3pc fiscal deficit target achievable, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia is capable of achieving its fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) under Budget 2027, provided the assumptions underpinning the budget hold amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, said Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz. He described Budget 2027 as a responsible budget that balances investment incentives with efforts to ensure that economic growth benefits a wider segment of Malaysians and businesses. On investment prospects, Tengku Zafrul said planned capital expenditure by government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) could generate positive spillover effects for the broader economy.

items.title: Senior govt agency official, company director remanded seven days in bribery probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — A senior official of a government agency and a company director have been remanded for seven days for allegedly soliciting and receiving bribes totalling about RM15,000. Magistrate Aliaa Anwar issued the remand order against both men, effective from today until Oct 19, following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court this morning. Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohammad Zakkuan Talib, when contacted, confirmed the remand.

items.title: STAM and MUET examinations in Pahang to continue as planned despite haze
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 13 — The Sijil Tinggi Agama Malaysia (STAM) and Malaysian University English Test (MUET) examinations in Pahang will proceed as scheduled despite the haze. In a statement, the Pahang State Education Department (JPN) said the examinations would be conducted in accordance with the standard operating procedures (SOP) and safety measures in force. Pahang JPN will continue to monitor the situation in coordination with the three district education offices and relevant agencies to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel.

items.title: Teachers union: RM69b education allocation must bring real improvements to Malaysian schools
items.summary: West Malaysia Malay Teachers Union (KGMMB) president Dr Mohd Sobri Yusuf said the RM69 billion allocation, up from RM66.2 billion this year, should translate into meaningful improvements in schools, with its success measured by the actual benefits delivered to teachers and students. Mohd Sobri said the higher school maintenance allocation, which has doubled to RM2 billion, could deliver direct benefits to school communities, particularly in ensuring that learning facilities were safe and comfortable. Mohd Sobri said the recruitment of 200 teaching assistants for primary schools with large numbers of pupils could help reduce teachers’ workload, allowing them to focus more on teaching and students’ learning needs.

items.title: Fahmi proposes initiative to preserve speeches, writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today has proposed a national initiative to preserve and revive historical speeches and writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders for future generations. He said the initiative, inspired by the reprint of pioneering journalist J. Victor Morais’ Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians, could involve retrieving rare speeches, writings and historical accounts from archives. Fahmi said this at the launch of Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians – A Reprint of Selected Speeches by Pioneering Journalist J. Victor Morais here today.

items.title: Orang Asli children should not be denied documentation over parents’ marriage records, says National Registration Dept
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 13 — Orang Asli children should not be left without documentation because of issues involving their parents’ marriage records, said National Registration Department (JPN) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias. He said JPN would assess each case based on the facts, supporting documents and individual circumstances to determine the appropriate action, particularly for birth registration. He said 143 New Generation MyKads had been issued to the Orang Asli community in Kelantan through the MEKAR Programme, which brings registration services closer to the community.

items.title: Body wrapped in cloth found in drain at Sama Gagah market in Penang
items.summary: Penang Police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng, when contacted by Bernama, confirmed the discovery and said investigations were underway to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and the cause of death. Several photographs showing the body had earlier gone viral on social media. — Bernama

items.title: MACC records RM1.27b in asset freezes from 2022 to September, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) recorded asset freezes worth RM1.27 billion from 2022 to September this year, involving bank accounts, jewellery, immovable property and other valuables. Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said the asset freezes were carried out under Section 44 of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613). He said 1,336 asset-freezing orders were issued under the Act in 2025, while another 1,006 were issued from Jan 1 to Sept 30 this year.

items.title: Budget 2027 should accelerate transition from R&D to Malaysian technology, says Mimos
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The government’s continued focus on strengthening the technology and innovation ecosystem through Budget 2027 provides an opportunity to accelerate the transition from research and development (R&D) to commercialisation, industry adoption and tangible economic value, said Mimos Bhd (Mimos). It said the government’s commitment to advancing Malaysia’s technology and innovation agenda, particularly through the Finance Ministry (MOF) and Science, Technology and Innovation Ministry (Mosti), would help strengthen the country’s R&D capabilities, develop home-grown technologies and translate innovation into economic and social benefits. Mimos President and Group Chief Executive Officer Dr Saat Shukri Embong said the next step for Malaysia is to ensure that these capabilities translate into commercial outcomes, stronger Malaysian intellectual property (IP), industry adoption and economic value.

items.title: Ministry to ensure Budget 2027 funds benefit women, children, OKU and elderly, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development’s (KPWKM) increased allocation under Budget 2027 will strengthen social protection and the well-being of target groups, including women, children, persons with disabilities (OKU) and the elderly. Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the funding, which rose four per cent to RM4.355 billion, would support various aid initiatives, the development of a care ecosystem and economic empowerment to help target groups realise their potential and become self-reliant. Nancy said the ministry is also focusing on women’s economic empowerment through an approach that combines skills, capital or equipment assistance, support networks and market opportunities to help them generate income.

items.title: Johor records nearly 10,000 commercial crime cases with RM212.64m in losses, says state top cop
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Johor police opened 9,897 investigation papers involving commercial crimes in the first nine months of this year, with losses totalling RM212.64 million. Its chief, Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad, said the figure represented an increase of 3,036 cases from the 6,861 recorded during the same period last year, although financial losses declined from RM252.57 million. Ab Rahaman said the state’s crime index also rose to 4,343 cases during the same period, compared with 4,152 last year.

items.title: King attends pre-council meeting of Conference of Rulers at Istana Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today attended the pre-council meeting of the 273rd Conference of Rulers at Istana Negara. According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page, the pre-council meeting was also attended by Tunku Temenggong Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj as the official representative of Johor Regent Tunku Mahkota Ismail. The 273rd Meeting of the Conference of Rulers will run for two days starting tomorrow and will be presided over by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of severe storms across peninsula and East Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across several states in Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah, forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 6pm today. In Kedah, stormy conditions are expected across eight districts: Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, Baling, Kuala Muda, Kulim, and Bandar Baharu. In Perak, the warning covers Kerian, Larut, Matang dan Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, and Perak Tengah.

items.title: Molotov cocktail attack on Kulai Rohingya settlement linked to provocative viral clip, police say
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Police believe an early morning arson attack targeting several homes at an ethnic Rohingya settlement in Kulai Besar was triggered by racially provocative videos circulating on social media. “Police have also received a report on the incident at 1.30am,” he said in a statement today. Ab Rahaman said police have launched investigations under both anti-arson statutes and cyber-crime laws.

items.title: Miri-Subang flights to begin Dec 1, offering new link to Klang Valley
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Miri residents will have another air travel option when a new flight service to Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport (LTSAAS) in Subang begins operations on December 1, 2026. Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said the new route would benefit residents who frequently travel for work, business, education, medical treatment and family commitments. He said improved air connectivity could benefit the business and tourism sectors while making travel between Miri and the Klang Valley more convenient.

items.title: Deputy minister: Anti-scalping provisions to be added to Price Control Act
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living is “actively” working on a dedicated legal framework to combat ticket scalping, with new regulations expected to take effect as early as next year, Parliament was told this morning. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Deputy Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh said anti-scalping provisions could be inserted under Section 15(1) of the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act, which grants authority to introduce measures curbing unfair pricing and resale practices. Fuziah said the anti-scalping provisions would include the definition of scalping itself, how to control bulk ticket purchasing activities and enforcing the use identification or names on ticket purchases.

items.title: Penang’s Jalan Magazine slip road to face periodic closures from Oct 14 until Feb 21 next year for Mutiara Line LRT works
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 13 — Part of the route along Jalan Magazine here will be closed periodically for 131 days starting tomorrow to make way for construction work on the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) Project. In a statement today, Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) said the long-term closure will start from 10am tomorrow and continue until 5am on February 21, 2027. MRT Corp said the closure will facilitate construction work on the Mutiara Line LRT Project under Package CMC1, including road widening and utility relocation works.

items.title: Malaysia’s semiconductor exports remain exempt from US tariffs, says Johari Ghani
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia continues to enjoy tariff exemptions for its semiconductor exports to the United States, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister (Miti) Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He said negotiations with the US under Section 301 covered four issues, namely forced labour, excess production capacity, the environmental standards and government subsidies. We do not have excess capacity,” said Johari.

items.title: Fadhlina: Schools in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and nine districts to close tomorrow as haze lingers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Schools in Johor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan will stay closed tomorrow, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek announced today, as haze continues to affect parts of the country. Schools under nine district education offices (PPD) in Selangor, Pahang, Sabah and Sarawak will also be shut. Today’s closures covered Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and Putrajaya, along with the Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat and Sepang PPDs in Selangor and the Kuantan and Rompin PPDs in Pahang.

items.title: Zahid: Malaysia and China ramp up fight against cyber scams, cross-border crime
items.summary: BEIJING, Oct 13 — Cross-border investigations and the recovery of assets stolen through cyber scams are among Malaysia’s key priorities in strengthening security cooperation with China, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said closer bilateral cooperation would help both countries tackle transnational crimes while delivering practical benefits under their comprehensive strategic partnership, particularly in security and law enforcement. The Deputy Prime Minister said Malaysia and China were also strengthening intelligence sharing and coordinating investigations and enforcement operations to combat cross-border crime.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Super El Nino forecast for March-May 2027, temperatures could break Malaysia’s 40.1°C record
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Malaysia needs to brace itself for the Super El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to bring scorching weather between March and May next year, potentially breaking the country’s record high temperature of 40.1 degrees Celsius. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the country’s maximum temperature could exceed 41 degrees Celsius, based on analysis of the current intense El Niño phenomenon, alongside the impacts of climate change and global warming. “If we look at current climate change trends, the rate of temperature increase in the country is approximately 0.13 degrees Celsius per decade.

items.title: Asyraf says BN’s Melaka seat talks 90pc complete, urges trust in Muslim political pact
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is in the final stages of seat negotiations for the Melaka state election, with the coalition aiming to defend the 21 state constituencies it secured in the previous polls. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the remaining deliberations focus on the seven remaining seats across the 28-seat state legislative assembly, with potential seat swaps actively under consideration, NST reported. “The negotiations have reached 90 per cent completion, with only 10 per cent remaining.

items.title: Lorry driver in Shah Alam 12-vehicle pile-up pleads not guilty to drug-impaired driving
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 13 — A lorry driver pleaded not guilty in the Magistrates’ Court here to driving against traffic under the influence of drugs and causing injuries to four other individuals last week. Agilan is accused of driving a lorry under the influence of methamphetamine and amphetamine, rendering him unable to control the vehicle and resulting in injuries to four individuals aged between 58 and 17. DPP Nur Amirah Zahari proposed bail of RM7,000, after which Rohan requested a minimum bail amount.
